sources.title: Interview note containing the file-backed Top-10 question
Deterministic Java validation against a full-sort-prefix oracle
Source-first isolated review for the file Top-K candidate

claims.text: The recovered source asks how to find the largest 10 numbers in a file of N numbers, while number format, duplicate semantics, malformed-row handling and N < 10 behavior are not preserved.
Maintaining at most K values in a min-heap and replacing the heap root only when a larger value arrives preserves the largest min(K, i) values of every processed input prefix.
The implementation scans the file once, performs at most one O(log K) heap update per value and retains at most K numeric candidates, giving O(N log K) time and O(K) candidate state.
The exact Java implementation passes seven fixed boundary families and 5000 deterministic randomized files against a full-sort-prefix oracle, plus malformed-row and invalid-K fail-fast checks.

checks: empty file, fewer-than-K and exactly-K inputs
5000 deterministic randomized files against a full-sort-prefix oracle

boundary_tests.expected: return all valid values in descending order
retain repeated occurrences when they belong to Top K
fail fast with NumberFormatException under the candidate parsing policy
Long.MIN_VALUE and Long.MAX_VALUE compare correctly without arithmetic overflow

findings: The candidate is source-bounded and separates recovered requirements from selected file/API policies.
The min-heap invariant and complexity claims match the Java implementation.
The independent oracle checks fixed edge cases and 5000 deterministic randomized inputs without reusing the heap algorithm.
Distinct-value semantics remain an explicit alternative policy instead of being silently imported into the source contract.
No unsupported production, online-judge or hidden-size claims were introduced.
Formal promotion remains blocked only by the pilot human-approval gate.
